patch.objective: How Google Cloud's global network -- regions, zones, and edge locations -- supports a digital transformation, and how the three relate

sources.cite: Google Cloud, Cloud Digital Leader exam guide (PDF, 'launched on August 12, 2026'): six sections, 18% each for the first five and 10% for Scaling with Google Cloud Operations
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-18; the section names and weights match the course seed. Bullet wording quoted from the HTML guide page (cloud.google.com/learn/certification/guides/cloud-digital-leader, read 2026-11-17): 1.2.e 'Discuss how Google Cloud supports digital transformation with global infrastructure and data centers connected by a fast, reliable network'; 2.1.b 'Differentiate between basic data management concepts, in particular: databases; data warehouses; data lakes'; 2.3.c 'Describe how streaming analytics in real time makes data more useful and generates business value'; 3.1.e 'Explain why high-quality, accurate data is essential for successful ML models'; 4.1.b 'Define the main cloud migration terms'. That HTML page showed weights of about 16-17% per section, which the PDF supersedes.

sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Backend services overview (Cloud Load Balancing)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17 (English page of the Google Cloud documentation mirror). Relevant text: the capacity scaler 'provides a way to scale the target capacity manually'; 0 means the backend is 'completely drained', 0.1 to 1.0 set the share of capacity in use; 0 cannot be used when the backend service has only one backend. The connection draining page (read 2026-11-18): when a backend is removed, 'existing, in-progress requests are given time to complete' and 'The load balancer doesn't send new connections to this VM or endpoint'. The error budget arithmetic is the author's.
